akhfash:18-18.t: He said ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمْ إِذَا جَآءَتْهُمْ ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾: He means "how will their reminder avail them when the Hour has come to them?"

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَن تُفْسِدُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: the first (إن تولّيتم) is for the conditional, and you made ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ fall on ﴿أَن تُفْسِدُواْ﴾ because it is a noun. ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ or "عَسَيْتُ" cannot operate on it unless "أنْ" is in it; you do not say "عَسَيْتُم الفِعْلَ" (you might the deed). Just as in your saying "لو ان زيدا جاء كان خيرا له" (if Zayd had come it would have been better for him), your saying "أَنَّ زَيْداً جاءَ" is a noun, yet you do not say "لوذاك" (if that), because not all nouns occur in every position, and not all verbs fall on all nouns. Do you not see that they say "يَدَعُ" (he leaves) but do not say "وَدَعَ", [and they say "يَذَرُ"] but do not say "وَذَر"?

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿وَلَن يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾, i.e. in your deeds, as you say: "دَخَلْتُ البيتَ" (I entered the house) while meaning "into the house".

akhfash:38-38.t: And He said ﴿هَا أَنتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ﴾: He put the alerting particle (hā) in two places for emphasis, and the alerting in "هَؤُلاَءِ" is a permanent alerting.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ others ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. faith ﴿أَضَلَّ﴾ He nullified ﴿أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ such as feeding people and maintaining ties of kinship; so they will see no reward for them in the Hereafter, and they are recompensed for them in this world out of His bounty, Exalted is He.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ i.e. the Anṣār and others ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ He forgave them ﴿سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ﴾ i.e. their state, so they do not disobey Him.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the nullifying of the deeds and the expiation of the evil deeds ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ because ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْبَاطِلَ﴾ Satan ﴿وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ﴾ the Quran ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like that explanation ﴿يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ﴾ He makes clear their states, i.e. the disbeliever's deeds come to nothing and the believer's slips are forgiven.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَضَرْبَ الرِّقَابِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the utterance of its verb, i.e. «فَاضْرِبُوا رِقَابَهُمْ» ("then strike their necks"), i.e. kill them; it is expressed as striking the necks because killing is mostly by striking the neck ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ you have killed many of them ﴿فَشُدُّوا﴾ i.e. then hold back from them, take them captive and tighten ﴿الْوَثَاقَ﴾ that with which captives are bound ﴿فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ﴾ a maṣdar standing in place of the utterance of its verb, i.e. you grant them favour by releasing them without anything in return ﴿وَإِمَّا فِدَاءً﴾ i.e. you ransom them for wealth or for Muslim captives ﴿حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ﴾ i.e. its people ﴿أَوْزَارَهَا﴾ its burdens of weapons and other things, by the disbelievers becoming Muslim or entering into a covenant; and this is the limit of the killing and capture ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «الْأَمْرُ فِيهِمْ مَا ذُكِرَ» ("the ruling concerning them is what has been mentioned") ﴿وَلَوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ لَانْتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ without fighting ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ He commanded you to do it ﴿لِيَبْلُوَ بَعْضَكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ of them in fighting, so that whoever of you is killed goes to the Garden and whoever of them to the Fire ﴿وَالَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا﴾ and in one reading [قَاتَلُوا]; the ayah was revealed on the day of Uḥud, when killing and wounds had spread among the Muslims ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ﴾ nullify ﴿أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿سَيَهْدِيهِمْ﴾ in this world and the Hereafter to what benefits them ﴿وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَهُمْ﴾ their state in both; what concerns this world is for those who were not killed, and they were included in «قُتِلُوا» by way of taghlīb (giving precedence to the predominant group).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَهَا﴾ He made it clear ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ so they are guided to their dwellings in it, their spouses and their servants without needing to seek direction.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَنْصُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. His religion and His Messenger ﴿يَنْصُرْكُمْ﴾ against your enemy ﴿وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ﴾ He makes you firm on the battlefield.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca; a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «تَعِسُوا» ("they are wretched"), indicated by ﴿فَتَعْسًا لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. destruction and failure from Allah ﴿وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to «تَعِسُوا».

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the wretchedness and the nullifying ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ كَرِهُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ of the Quran, which contains the obligations ﴿فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ He destroyed them, their children and their wealth ﴿وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ أَمْثَالُهَا﴾ i.e. the like of the end of those before them.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the help given to the believers and the subjugation of the disbelievers ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى﴾ the protector and helper of ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ لَا مَوْلَى لَهُمْ﴾.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ﴾ in this world ﴿وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَمَا تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعَامُ﴾ i.e. they have no concern except their bellies and their private parts, and they pay no attention to the Hereafter ﴿وَالنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. a lodging, an abode and a destination.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾ how many ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ by which its people are meant ﴿هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ﴾ the people of Mecca ﴿الَّتِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ﴾ the wording of «قَرْيَة» is observed ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ﴾ the meaning of the first «قَرْيَة» is observed ﴿فَلَا نَاصِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ from Our destroying them.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ كَانَ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ a proof and demonstration ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ and they are the believers ﴿كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ﴾ so he saw it as good, and they are the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ in the worship of idols; i.e. there is no likeness between the two.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ i.e. the description of ﴿الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾ shared among those who enter it; a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿فِيهَا أَنْهَارٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ﴾ with the long vowel and the short, like «ضَارِب» and «حَذِر», i.e. unchanging, unlike the water of this world, which changes through some accident ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ﴾ unlike the milk of this world, because it comes out of udders ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ لَذَّةٍ﴾ delicious ﴿لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ unlike the wine of this world, for it is unpleasant when drunk ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِنْ عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى﴾ unlike the honey of this world, for on coming out of the bee's belly it mixes with wax and other things ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ kinds ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ so He is pleased with them along with His bestowing on them what has been mentioned, unlike the master of slaves in this world, for he may, along with his kindness to them, be displeased with them ﴿كَمَنْ هُوَ خَالِدٌ فِي النَّارِ﴾ the khabar of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ, i.e. «أَمَنْ هُوَ فِي هَذَا النَّعِيمِ» ("is the one who is in this bliss…") ﴿وَسُقُوا مَاءً حَمِيمًا﴾ i.e. intensely hot ﴿فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعَاءَهُمْ﴾ i.e. their intestines, so they come out of their rear ends; it is the plural of «مِعًى» with the short alif, and its alif comes from a yāʾ, because they say «مِعْيَانِ» (in the dual).

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ in the Friday sermon, and they are the hypocrites ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ قَالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ to the learned among the Companions, among them Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, in mockery and ridicule: ﴿مَاذَا قَالَ آنِفًا﴾ with the long vowel and the short, i.e. just now; i.e. we do not pay heed to him ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ with disbelief ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ in hypocrisy.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا﴾ and they are the believers ﴿زَادَهُمْ﴾ Allah ﴿هُدًى وَآتَاهُمْ تَقْوَاهُمْ﴾ He inspired them with that by which they guard themselves against the Fire.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ they are not waiting, i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of «السَّاعَةَ», i.e. the matter is nothing but that it should come to them ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly ﴿فَقَدْ جَاءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا﴾ its signs, among them the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, the splitting of the moon, and the smoke ﴿فَأَنَّى لَهُمْ إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ﴾ the Hour ﴿ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾ their remembering, i.e. it will not benefit them.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. persist, O Muhammad, in your knowledge of that, which is beneficial on the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ﴾ for its sake; this was said to him despite his infallibility so that his community would follow his practice in it, and he did it: he ﷺ said, "Indeed I seek Allah's forgiveness every day a hundred times" ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ in it is an honouring of them, by their Prophet being commanded to seek forgiveness for them ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ﴾ your going about your occupations in the daytime ﴿وَمَثْوَاكُمْ﴾ your retiring to your beds at night; i.e. He knows all your states, nothing of them is hidden from Him, so beware of Him. The address is to the believers and others.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ seeking jihad ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why has not ﴿نُزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾ in which jihad is mentioned ﴿فَإِذَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُحْكَمَةٌ﴾ i.e. nothing of it has been abrogated ﴿وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا الْقِتَالُ﴾ i.e. the demand for it ﴿رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ i.e. doubt, and they are the hypocrites ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ نَظَرَ الْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ out of fear of it and aversion to it; i.e. they fear fighting and hate it ﴿فَأَوْلَى لَهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿طَاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ﴾ i.e. good, to you ﴿فَإِذَا عَزَمَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ i.e. fighting was made obligatory ﴿فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in faith and obedience ﴿لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾ and the «لَوْ» clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا».

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿فَهَلْ عَسِيتُمْ﴾ with kasra on the sīn and with fatḥa [عَسَيْتُمْ]; in it is iltifāt (a shift) from the third person to direct address; i.e. perhaps you ﴿إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ turned away from faith ﴿أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ﴾ i.e. you would return to the ways of the Jāhiliyya of aggression and fighting.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ i.e. the corrupters ﴿الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ﴾ from hearing the truth ﴿وَأَعْمَى أَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾ to the path of guidance.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ so that they would recognise the truth ﴿أَمْ﴾ rather ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبٍ﴾ of theirs ﴿أَقْفَالُهَا﴾ so they do not understand it.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ارْتَدُّوا﴾ through hypocrisy ﴿عَلَى أَدْبَارِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْهُدَى الشَّيْطَانُ سَوَّلَ﴾ i.e. made attractive ﴿لَهُمْ وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ﴾ with ḍamma on its first letter, and with fatḥa on it and on the lām [وَأَمْلَى]; the one granting respite is Satan, by the will of Allah the Exalted, so He is the One who leads them astray.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. their being led astray ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُوا مَا نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. to the idolaters ﴿سَنُطِيعُكُمْ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ﴾ i.e. cooperating in enmity to the Prophet ﷺ and in holding people back from jihad with him; they said that secretly, and Allah the Exalted exposed it ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَسْرَارَهُمْ﴾ with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of «سِرّ» (secret), and with kasra on it [إِسْرَارَهُمْ], a maṣdar (verbal noun).

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ will be their state ﴿إِذَا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْمَلَائِكَةُ» ﴿وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ﴾ their backs, with maces of iron.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the taking of their souls in the state mentioned ﴿بِأَنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا مَا أَسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوَانَهُ﴾ i.e. doing what pleases Him ﴿فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أَنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغَانَهُمْ﴾ expose their rancour against the Prophet ﷺ and the believers.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَاءُ لَأَرَيْنَاكَهُمْ﴾ We would have made them known to you; and the lām is repeated in ﴿فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾ their mark ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is for an omitted oath and what follows it is its answer ﴿فِي لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ﴾ i.e. its meaning, when they speak in your presence, by hinting at what disparages the affair of the Muslims ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ﴾ We shall surely test you with jihad and other things ﴿حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ﴾ with a knowledge of manifestation ﴿الْمُجَاهِدِينَ مِنْكُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in jihad and other things ﴿وَنَبْلُوَا﴾ make manifest ﴿أَخْبَارَكُمْ﴾ of your obedience and your disobedience in jihad and other things; with yāʾ and with nūn in the three verbs.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ the path of truth ﴿وَشَاقُّوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ opposed him ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْهُدَى﴾ it is the meaning of «سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ» ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئًا وَسَيُحْبِطُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ He will invalidate them, such as charity and the like, so they will see no reward for them in the Hereafter. It was revealed concerning those of the people of Badr who fed [the army], or concerning Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَلَا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾ by acts of disobedience, for example.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His path, and it is guidance ﴿ثُمَّ مَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾ it was revealed concerning the people of the well (al-qalīb) [at Badr].

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿فَلَا تَهِنُوا﴾ do not weaken ﴿وَتَدْعُوا إِلَى السَّلْمِ﴾ with fatḥa and with kasra on the sīn, i.e. peace with the disbelievers when you meet them ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ﴾ the wāw that is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) has been dropped from it; the most dominant, the overpowering ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾ with aid and help ﴿وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ﴾ He will not diminish for you ﴿أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾ i.e. their reward.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ i.e. being occupied in it ﴿لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ Allah, and that is among the matters of the Hereafter ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ أُجُورَكُمْ وَلَا يَسْأَلْكُمْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ﴾ all of it, but only the zakat prescribed in it.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿إِنْ يَسْأَلْكُمُوهَا فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾ press you hard in demanding it ﴿تَبْخَلُوا وَيُخْرِجْ﴾ the stinginess ﴿أَضْغَانَكُمْ﴾ toward the religion of Islam.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ﴾ O ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ what has been made obligatory on you ﴿فَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَبْخَلُ وَمَنْ يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّمَا يَبْخَلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ one says «بَخِلَ عَلَيْهِ» and «بَخِلَ عَنْهُ» ﴿وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ in no need of your spending ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ﴾ in need of Him ﴿وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ from obeying Him ﴿يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ i.e. He will make them your replacement ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ﴾ in turning away from obeying Him, but rather obedient to Him, Mighty and Majestic is He.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ conjoined to kafarū. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَضَلَّ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of alladhīna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to āmanū. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَآمَنُوا﴾ conjoined. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what precedes them. ﴿نُزِّلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ its khabar. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is parenthetical and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَّرَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of alladhīna. ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to kaffara ʿanhum. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the ṣila. ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of anna. ﴿الْباطِلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يَضْرِبُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَمْثالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:4-6.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿لَقِيتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَضَرْبَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿الرِّقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَشُدُّوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْوَثاقَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption and of consequence (tafrīʿ), and immā is a particle of condition and of detailing (tafṣīl). ﴿مَنًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿بَعْدُ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿وَإِمَّا فِداءً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حَتَّى تَضَعَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā. ﴿الْحَرْبُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَوْزارَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) fidāʾ. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَانْتَصَرَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal). ﴿لِيَبْلُوَا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), with its fāʿil latent. ﴿بَعْضَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِبَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and they are attached to an implied, omitted verb. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿قُتِلُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a ḍamma (اللَّهُ); as muḍāf ilayhi it is اللَّهِ.] ﴿فَلَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and lan is a particle causing the accusative. ﴿يُضِلَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by lan, its fāʿil latent. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿سَيَهْدِيهِمْ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَيُصْلِحُ بالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to sa-yahdīhim. ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ﴾ conjoined to sa-yahdīhim. ﴿الْجَنَّةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَرَّفَها﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-janna.

daas-irab:7-11.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ yā is a vocative particle, hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ayy is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَنْصُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَنْصُرْكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is its object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to yanṣurkum. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَتَعْساً﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) taʿsan. ﴿وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ a preposition, and anna and its noun. ﴿كَرِهُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause karihū is the khabar (predicate) of anna. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْزَلَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to karihū. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lam is a particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَسِيرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَيَنْظُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَيْفَ كانَ﴾ an interrogative noun, the fronted khabar of kāna. ﴿عاقِبَةُ﴾ its postponed noun. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [element that is the] ṣila of the relative noun; the clause kāna stands in place of the object of yanẓurū. ﴿دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿أَمْثالُها﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna, and the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and they are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَنَّ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, which works like inna. ﴿مَوْلَى﴾ its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ conjoined to āmanū. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of jannāt. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَتَمَتَّعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of alladhīna. ﴿وَيَأْكُلُونَ﴾ conjoined to yatamattaʿūna. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and of the genitive, and mā is maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَأْكُلُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْأَنْعامُ﴾ fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَالنَّارُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَثْوىً﴾ its khabar. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to mathwan; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and kaʾayyin is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿قَرْيَةٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification), genitive in form. ﴿هِيَ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz; the clause kaʾayyin is resumptive, and the clause hiya ashaddu is an adjective of qarya. ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ashaddu. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of qaryatika. ﴿أَخْرَجَتْكَ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the khabar of kaʾayyin. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and lā is the lā of generic negation, which works like inna. ﴿ناصِرَ﴾ its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and man is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is latent. ﴿عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of kāna; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of bayyina. ﴿كَمَنْ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ man. ﴿زُيِّنَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سُوءُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَمَلِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verbal clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of al-janna. ﴿وُعِدَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيها﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْهارٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of anhār. ﴿غَيْرِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿آسِنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause fīhā anhār is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ mathal. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam. ﴿طَعْمُهُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective of laban. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَذَّةٍ﴾ an adjective of khamr. ﴿لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ an adjective of ladhdha. ﴿وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى﴾ conjoined to the one before it. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and lahum is a fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of the omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الثَّمَراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and maghfira is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of maghfira. ﴿كَمَنْ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُوَ خالِدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khālid. ﴿وَسُقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿ماءٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (ماءٍ); in the verse it is the accusative ماءً.] ﴿حَمِيماً﴾ an adjective of māʾ; the clause is conjoined to the ṣila clause. ﴿فَقَطَّعَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَمْعاءَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and minhum is a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿خَرَجُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿الْعِلْمَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ماذا﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila, on the view that dhā is a relative noun. ﴿آنِفاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿طَبَعَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اهْتَدَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿زادَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿هُدىً﴾ its second object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَآتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, its fāʿil being latent. ﴿تَقْواهُمْ﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿السَّاعَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of al-sāʿa. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَ أَشْراطُها﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is causal and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and annā is an interrogative noun, the fronted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "deliverance" (al-khalāṣ). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿جاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْراهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its object and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَاعْلَمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لا إِلهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 8 of al-Dukhān; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna, the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of iʿlam, and the clause iʿlam is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِذَنْبِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ﴾ its object. ﴿وَمَثْواكُمْ﴾ conjoined to it; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:20-23.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of alladhīna. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿نُزِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أُنْزِلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿مُحْكَمَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَذُكِرَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿فِيهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْقِتالُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿نَظَرَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿الْمَغْشِيِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to al-maghshiyy. ﴿مِنَ الْمَوْتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to it. ﴿فَأَوْلى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and awlā is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the past, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it. ﴿طاعَةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿وَقَوْلٌ﴾ conjoined to ṭāʿa. ﴿مَعْرُوفٌ﴾ an adjective of qawl. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿عَزَمَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَلَوْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle falling in the apodosis of idhā, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿صَدَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَكانَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of law, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ its khabar. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the clause la-kāna is the apodosis of law and has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source reads «جواب لولا محل لها», evidently «جواب لو لا محل لها» run together.] ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿عَسَيْتُمْ﴾ ʿasā and its noun. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is its fāʿil; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position, and the clause ʿasaytum is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحامَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to an tufsidū; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the khabar of ʿasā. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَعَنَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَأَصَمَّهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَعْمى أَبْصارَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to fa-aṣammahum.

daas-irab:24-28.t: ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lā is negative. ﴿يَتَدَبَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَقْفالُها﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿ارْتَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَبَيَّنَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْهُدَى﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿سَوَّلَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَأَمْلى لَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to sawwala lahum. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كَرِهُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿سَنُطِيعُكُمْ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فِي بَعْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَمْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِسْرارَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an interrogative noun, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿تَوَفَّتْهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وُجُوهَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَدْبارَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to wujūhahum; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا﴾ see verse 26. ﴿ما أَسْخَطَ﴾ mā is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:29-31.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, lightened from the heavy anna; its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. ﴿لَنْ يُخْرِجَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿أَضْغانَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar of an, and an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in place of the two objects of ḥasiba. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَأَرَيْناكَهُمْ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the kāf is its first object and the hāʾ its second object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, the lām falls in the apodosis of law, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām falls in the answer to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي لَحْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām falls in the answer to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of causation (taʿlīl) and of the genitive. ﴿نَعْلَمَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after ḥattā, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْمُجاهِدِينَ﴾ its object; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what precedes them; the clause la-nabluwannakum is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to al-mujāhidīn. ﴿وَالصَّابِرِينَ﴾ conjoined to al-mujāhidīn. ﴿وَنَبْلُوَا﴾ conjoined to naʿlama. ﴿أَخْبارَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:32-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ conjoined to kafarū. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَشَاقُّوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ﴾ ﴿بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shāqqū. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿تَبَيَّنَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it. ﴿الْهُدى﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as mafʿūl bihi it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for an absolute object). ﴿وَسَيُحْبِطُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ refer to verse no. 7. ﴿أَطِيعُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تُبْطِلُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ see verse no. 34. [Translator's note: so in the source; this is verse 34 itself, and the parallel analysis is in verse 32 above.] ﴿وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ماتُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by lan, and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as fāʿil it is اللَّهُ.] ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna alladhīna is initial.

daas-irab:35-37.t: ﴿فَلا تَهِنُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَدْعُوا﴾ conjoined to tahinū. ﴿إِلَى السَّلْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan; the kāf is its first object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لَعِبٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَلَهْوٌ﴾ conjoined to laʿib; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and in causes the jussive. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ conjoined to tuʾminū. ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is latent and the kāf is its first object. ﴿أُجُورَكُمْ﴾ its second object; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا يَسْئَلْكُمْ أَمْوالَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and yasʾalkum amwālakum is conjoined to yuʾtikum ujūrakum. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَسْئَلْكُمُوها﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis; its fāʿil is latent, the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and hā the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial. ﴿فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb conjoined to yasʾalkumūhā. ﴿تَبْخَلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُخْرِجْ﴾ conjoined to tabkhalū. ﴿أَضْغانَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ها﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿تُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِتُنْفِقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) tudʿawna. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَمِنْكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption and of consequence (tafrīʿ), and minkum is a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and innamā is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يَبْخَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ and al-ghaniyy its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ﴾ conjoined to Allāhu al-ghaniyy. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial. ﴿يَسْتَبْدِلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive, and its noun. ﴿أَمْثالَكُمْ﴾ its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُحَمَّدٍ) An Arabic name, on the pattern mufaʿʿal from al-ḥamd (praise); the doubling in it is for frequency, as you say "I honoured him (karramtuhu), so he is mukarram" and "I glorified him, so he is muʿaẓẓam" when you have done that time after time. It is transferred from the adjective, by way of good omen that his praise would be abundant — and so he was ﷺ. Some transmitters of knowledge narrated, in what Ibn Durayd related, that when the Prophet ﷺ was born, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ordered a camel to be slaughtered, and it was slaughtered, and he invited the men of Quraysh. It was their custom with a newborn, if he was born at the onset of night, to turn a cooking pot over him until morning. They did that with the Prophet ﷺ, and in the morning the pot had split open from over him and he was gazing up at the sky. When the men of Quraysh came and had eaten, they said to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: "What have you named this son of yours?"
He said: "I have named him Muḥammad." They said: "This is not one of the names of your forefathers." He said: "I wanted him to be praised in the heavens and the earth." One says: a man maḥmūd (praised) and muḥammad. Al-Aʿshā said:
إليك أبيت اللعن كان كلالها ... إلى الواحد الفرد الجواد المحمّد
(To you — may you be spared the curse — was her weariness [spent], to the one, the unique, the generous, the much-praised.)
So maḥmūd does not indicate abundance, while muḥammad indicates it; and what indicates the difference between them is the poet's saying:
فلست بمحمود ولا بمحمد ... ولكنما أنت الحبط الحباتر
(You are neither praised nor much-praised; you are only the bloated, stunted one.)
The Arabs in the Jāhiliyya named some of their sons with it, among them: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān al-Juʿfī, the poet, who lived in the time of Imruʾ al-Qays and whom he called "Shuwayʿir" (the little poet); Muḥammad ibn Khawlī al-Hamdānī; Muḥammad ibn Bilāl ibn Uḥayḥa, who was the husband of Salmā bint ʿAmr, the grandmother of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mother of his grandfather; Muḥammad ibn Sufyān ibn Mujāshiʿ ibn Dārim; Muḥammad ibn Maslama al-Anṣārī; and Abū Muḥammad ibn Aws ibn Zayd, who was present at Badr.
(بالَهُمْ) Al-bāl: the heart — one says "the matter did not occur to my mind (bi-bālī)"; state and living — one says "so-and-so is of easy bāl"; the mind — one says "so-and-so is of downcast bāl"; and what one is concerned with — one says "this is not of my bāl", i.e. of what I care about; "a matter of bāl", i.e. one that is attended to; and "mā bāluka", i.e. what is your affair? Al-Jawharī said: «Al-bāl is also the ease of living; one says "so-and-so is rakhiyy al-bāl", i.e. of easy living.» The wording of al-Bayḍāwī: «(وأصلح بالهم), i.e. their state in religion and in this world, through granting success and support.» The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «Al-bāl is thought; you say "such-and-such occurred in my bāl". It is not put into the dual or plural, and their saying bālāt as its plural is anomalous.» The wording of al-Qāmūs: «Al-bāl: state, mind, heart, and the great whale; and with tāʾ marbūṭa [bāla]: the flask, the leather bag, and the perfume container.»
(أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ) You have inflicted much slaughter on them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Athkhana fī al-arḍ ithkhānan: he marched against the enemy and slaughtered them widely; and athkhantuhu: I weakened him with wounds and enfeebled him.»
(الْوَثاقَ) With fatḥa and kasra: the name of that by which something is bound. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-wathāq is the fetter, the rope and the like, with fatḥa or kasra on the wāw; the plural is wuthuq, like ribāṭ / rubuṭ and ʿanāq / ʿunuq.»
(أَوْزارَها) Its implements and burdens without which it cannot stand, such as weapons and horses. Al-Aʿshā said:
وأعددت للحرب أوزارها ... رماحا طوالا وخيلا ذكورا
(And I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and stallion horses.)
The wording of al-Kashshāf: «They were called its awzār because, since it cannot do without dragging them, it is as though it carries them and bears them; and when it ends, it is as though it has laid them down. It was also said that its awzār are its sins, meaning: until the people of war, who are the polytheists, abandon their polytheism and their sins by embracing Islam.»

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (صدّوا) is conjoined to (كفروا); (عن سبيل الله) are attached to (صدّوا). (أضلّ أعمالهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to Allah the Exalted, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of (الذين). Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted (الذين) to be accusative by a verb indicated by what is mentioned, i.e. "He led astray those who disbelieved". (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِما نُزِّلَ عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا), and (آمنوا بما نزل على محمد) is also conjoined. The wāw is parenthetical; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الحق) its khabar; and (من ربهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ) The clause (كفّر عنهم) is the khabar of (الذين آمنوا); (سيئاتهم) is a direct object; and (أصلح بالهم) is conjoined to (كفّر عنهم سيئاتهم). (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْباطِلَ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأن الذين كفروا) its khabar; and the clause (اتبعوا الباطل) is the khabar of (أن). (وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) Conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab has been given. (كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثالَهُمْ) (كذلك) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. like that striking [of examples] Allah strikes for people their examples. The meaning of striking the example here will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَإِذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the command within its domain consequent on what precedes it. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; what governs it is an implied verb, which is also what governs (ضرب الرقاب), its implied form being "then strike the necks at the time of your meeting the enemy"; the maṣdar itself does not govern it because it is emphatic. The clause (لقيتم) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الذين) is the object of (لقيتم), and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila. The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; (ضرب) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and (الرقاب) is muḍāf ilayhi. (حَتَّى إِذا أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ فَشُدُّوا الْوَثاقَ فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِداءً) (حتى) is a particle of inception, i.e. clauses begin after it; Abū Ḥayyān made it a particle of limit and of the genitive, saying: «And this is a limit for the striking.» (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (أثخنتموهم) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (شدّوا الوثاق) is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object. The fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); (إما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (منّا) and (فداء) are two maṣdars made accusative by a verb that may not be made overt, because when a maṣdar is brought to detail the outcome of a clause, it must be accusative by an implied verb; the implied form is "either you show favour (tamunnū) as a favour, or you ransom (tufādū) as a ransom". Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted them to be two direct objects of an implied governing word, its implied form being "grant them a favour and accept from them a ransom" — and that is not the right view. (بعد) is an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. after capturing them and tightening their bonds. (حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها) (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; together with what it governs it is attached either to the striking and the binding, or to the favour and the ransom, because it is a limit for all of that, according to a detailed discussion you will find set out at length in the books of the jurists — this is not its place. More explanation will come in the section on Rhetoric. (تضع) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after (حتى); (الحرب) is the agent and (أوزارها) a direct object. (ذلِكَ وَلَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَانْتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَا بَعْضَكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ) (ذلك) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the matter concerning them is what has been mentioned of killing and capture and what follows of favour and ransom; you may also make it accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "do that". The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (يشاء الله) is an imperfect verb and its agent; the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); (انتصر) is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "He", i.e. Allah the Exalted. (ولكن): the wāw is a conjunction or of ḥāl, and (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened. The lām is causal; (يبلو) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the lām and what it governs are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He commanded you to fight"; (بعضكم) is a direct object, and (ببعض) are attached to (يبلو). (وَالَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (قتلوا) is the ṣila; (في سبيل الله) are attached to (قتلوا). The fāʾ is linking, because of the sense of condition in the relative noun; (لن) is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; (يضل) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن), its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (أعمالهم) is a direct object; and the clause is the khabar of (الذين). (سَيَهْدِيهِمْ وَيُصْلِحُ بالَهُمْ) The sīn is a particle of the future; (يهديهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (يصلح) is conjoined to (يهدي), and (بالهم) is a direct object. (وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَها لَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (يدخلهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (الجنة) is a second direct
object, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and the clause (عرفها لهم) is resumptive or circumstantial. The meaning of (عرفها لهم) will come in the section on Benefits.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words, Exalted is He, «وأضلّ أعمالهم» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): He likened their deeds to stray camels that are left to perish, with no owner to guard them and look after them; or to water that gets lost in milk. The meaning is that the good deeds of the disbelievers were lost amid the whole of their evil deeds of disbelief and sins, until their good became consumed in the flood of their evil. Its counterpart for the believers is Allah's covering of their evil deeds within the shelter of their good deeds of faith and obedience, until their evil became expiated and effaced beside the good of their deeds. To this beautiful illustration of not accepting the good of the disbelievers and of overlooking the evil deeds of the believers the allusion was made in His words, Exalted is He, «كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم». The detail of that is that striking an example is the use of a current saying whose occasion of application is likened to its original occasion. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: where is the striking of examples? I say: in His making the following of falsehood an example for the deeds of the disbelievers and the following of truth an example for the deeds of the believers; or in making the leading astray an example for the failure of the disbelievers, and the expiation of evil deeds an example for the triumph of the believers.»
2- The synecdochic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words, Exalted is He, «فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب» there is a majāz mursal whose relation is mentioning the part and meaning the whole, because striking the necks is an expression for killing; but since a person is most often killed by striking his neck, it came to be an expression for killing. The trope was preferred for the depiction and embodiment it contains, because in this expression — as al-Zamakhsharī says — there is a harshness and severity not found in the word "killing", since it depicts killing in its most hideous form, namely cutting the neck and sending flying the member which is the head of the body, its highest part and the most prominent of its members.
3- In His words, Exalted is He, «حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها» there is an implicit or explicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya or taṣrīḥiyya). On the first, war is likened to riding-beasts bearing awzār, i.e. heavy loads; on the second, awzār is borrowed for the implements of war. There is also in it a trope in attribution (majāz fī al-isnād), for the laying down of burdens is attributed to the war, whereas it belongs only to its people.

* Benefits:
The meaning of His words, Exalted is He, «عرّفها لهم» is either from taʿrīf in the sense of delimiting, such that each one has a Garden set apart — and in al-Bukhārī there is what indicates the soundness of this view, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The believers will be delivered from the Fire, then they will be held on a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, until, when they have been refined and purified, they will be permitted to enter the Garden. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, each of them will be better guided to his dwelling in the Garden than to his dwelling that he had in this world»; or it is from al-ʿarf, which is fragrance. Ibn ʿAbbās said: He perfumed it for them with kinds of delights; and "a muʿarraf food", i.e. a seasoned one. The Arabs say: "ʿarraftu al-qidr" when you have seasoned the pot with salt and spices. And in the speech of one of them: "ʿazfun ka-nawḥ al-qamārī wa-ʿarfun ka-fawḥ al-qamārī" (a melody like the cooing of the turtle-doves, and a fragrance like the diffusing of the qamārī [aloes]); the first qamārī is the plural of qumrī, the name of a bird, and the second qamārī is an aloeswood attributed to a place in the land of India. So it is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ.

dervis-irab:7-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَعْساً) Al-taʿs: perishing and the frustration of hope. In al-Mukhtār: «Al-taʿs is perishing; its origin is falling on one's face (al-kabb), and it is the opposite of recovering (al-intiʿāsh). Taʿasa, of the pattern qaṭaʿa, and Allah made him perish (atʿasahu); and one says "taʿsan li-fulān", i.e. may Allah make perishing binding on him.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Taʿisa taʿasan, of the pattern taʿiba, is a dialectal form, so he is taʿis like taʿib; it is made transitive by the vowel and by the hamza, so one says "Allah taʿasahu" with fatḥa, and "atʿasahu". In supplication: "taʿsan lahu", and "taʿisa wa-ntakasa" (may he fall and relapse): al-taʿs is that he falls on his face, and al-naks is that he does not get up after his fall until he falls a second time, which is worse than the first.» In al-Asās: «Taʿasa fulān, with fatḥa — kasra is not eloquent — and "taʿsan lahu", and Allah taʿasahu and atʿasahu. He said:
غداة هزمنا جمعهم بمقالع ... فآبوا بأتعاس على شر طائر
(The morning we routed their host with slings, so they returned in ruin under the worst of omens.)
And you say: "may Allah lower his cheek and ruin his fortune"; he is manḥūs mutʿūs (ill-starred and ruined); and this matter is a cause of ruin and ill-luck (mataʿsa manḥasa).» The wording of al-Qurṭubī: «There are ten views on al-taʿs. The first: remoteness, said by Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jurayj. The second: disgrace to them, said by al-Suddī. The third: wretchedness to them, said by Ibn Zayd. The fourth: a reviling of them from Allah, said by al-Ḥasan. The fifth: perishing to them, said by Thaʿlab. The sixth: frustration to them, said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Ziyād. The seventh: ugliness to them, related by al-Naqqāsh. The eighth: humiliation to them, also said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk. The ninth: evil to them, also said by Thaʿlab. The tenth: misery to them, said by Abū al-ʿĀliya.»

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَنْصُرُوا اللَّهَ يَنْصُرْكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَكُمْ) (يا أيها الذين آمنوا): its i'rab has been given many times. (إن) is conditional; (تنصروا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الله) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ينصركم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (يثبت أقدامكم) is conjoined to the apodosis. A muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "the religion of Allah and His Messenger". (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَتَعْساً لَهُمْ وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "they were ruined (taʿisū)", and it is what governs (تعسا); it may also be accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows it. The clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the fāʾ is linking, by likening the relative noun to a condition; (تعسا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, as above; (لهم) are attached to (تعسا), or are an adjective of it; and (أضل أعمالهم) is conjoined to the verb that made (تعسا) accusative. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَرِهُوا ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأنهم) its khabar; (أن) and its noun, and the clause (كرهوا) is its khabar; (ما) is a direct object, and the clause (أنزل الله) is the ṣila. (فأحبط) is conjoined to (كرهوا), and (أعمالهم) is a direct object. (أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يسيروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (في الأرض) are attached to (يسيروا). (فينظروا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and (ينظروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of (كان); (عاقبة) is its postponed noun; (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (من قبلهم) are attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. (دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ أَمْثالُها) The clause explains (كيف) and has no grammatical position. (دمر الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (عليهم) are attached to (دمر); and the object of (دمر) is omitted, its implied form being "He destroyed their selves, their wealth and what they had built"; you may also make (دمر) carry the meaning of "was wrathful", so that it needs no object. (للكافرين) is a fronted khabar and (أمثالها) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the pronoun refers back to the aforementioned outcome, i.e. the likes of the outcome of those before them; it may also refer to the destruction understood from His words (دمر الله عليهم), but the first is preferable. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الْكافِرِينَ لا مَوْلى لَهُمْ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأن) its khabar; (الله) is the noun of (أن), and (مولى الذين آمنوا) is the khabar of (أن). (وأن الكافرين) is conjoined to what preceded; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (مولى) is its noun and (لهم) its khabar; and the clause is the khabar of (أن). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) The clause explains His guardianship, Exalted is He, and what follows from it. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يدخل الذين آمنوا) is its khabar; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila and falls within its domain; (جنات) is a second direct object, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is an adjective of (جنات). (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَما تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعامُ وَالنَّارُ مَثْوىً لَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; the clause (يتمتعون) is the khabar of (الذين); the clause (يأكلون) is conjoined to the clause (يتمتعون). (كما) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), according to the school of most grammarians, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), according to the school of Sībawayh. (تأكل الأنعام) is a verb and its agent. The wāw is resumptive; (النار) is a mubtadaʾ, (مثوى) a khabar, and (لهم) an adjective of (مثوى).

dervis-irab:13-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آسِنٍ) With the long and the short vowel [āsin / asin], like ḍārib and ḥadhir; i.e. unaltered, unlike the water of this world, which changes because of the accidents that befall it. In al-Mukhtār: «Al-āsin, of water, is like al-ājin in form and meaning (stagnant, brackish); asana, of the pattern ḍaraba and dakhala; and asina, so it is āsin, of the pattern ṭariba, is a dialectal form of it.» One says: the water asana and ajana when its taste and smell change. A verse by Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya was recited:
لقد سقتني رضابا غير ذي أسن ... كالمسك فتّ على ماء العناقيد
(She gave me to drink a saliva without staleness, like musk crumbled onto the juice of grape clusters.)
(عَسَلٍ) They transmitted both masculine and feminine for al-ʿasal (honey), and in the Quran it comes as masculine in His words (من عسل مصفى). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-ʿasal is masculine and feminine — and that is the more common — and its diminutive is ʿusayla, according to the feminine usage, on the view that it is a portion of the genus and a part of it.» In al-Mukhtār: «Al-ʿasal is masculine and feminine; from it one says ʿasala al-ṭaʿām, i.e. he prepared it with honey, of the patterns ḍaraba and naṣara; zanjabīl muʿassal, i.e. ginger prepared with honey; al-ʿāsil is the one who takes honey from the beehive; and the bees are ʿassāla.» In al-Asās: «The guide trots (yaʿsilu) in the desert; the winds struck the water so that it ripples (yaʿsilu ʿasalānan). Al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
قد صبّحت والظل غض ما رحل ... حوضا كأن ماءه إذا عسل
من نافض الريح رويزيّ سمل
(She came in the morning, while the shade was still fresh and had not departed, to a trough whose water, when it rippled from the shaking of the wind, was like a worn Rūzī garment.)
A quivering spear and a trotting wolf (ʿassāl), and quivering spears and trotting wolves (ʿawāsil). And you say: "the trotting one gathers in the shade as the honey-gatherer collects the honey"; and "the Banū so-and-so hasten to the ʿassāla as the bees speed to the ʿassāla", which is the hive. Food maʿsūl and muʿassal; and ʿasaltu al-qawm and ʿassaltuhum: I fed them honey.»

* I'rab:
(وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْناهُمْ فَلا ناصِرَ لَهُمْ) Resumptive speech, introduced to console him ﷺ, serving as an example for him. (كأين) is predicative (khabariyya); it is a word compounded of the kāf and (أي), in the sense of the predicative kam, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (من قرية) is its tamyīz (specification) — the discussion of it has been given in detail before, so refresh your memory of it. (هي) is a mubtadaʾ and (أشد) a khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective of (قرية); (قوة) is a tamyīz; (من قريتك) are attached to (أشد); (التي) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قريتك), and the clause (أخرجتك) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (التي). The clause (أهلكناهم) is the khabar of (كأين). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ناصر) is its noun and (لهم) its khabar. From Ibn ʿAbbās: when the Prophet ﷺ left Mecca for the cave, he turned towards Mecca and said: «You are the dearest of Allah's lands to me, and were it not that your people drove me out of you, I would not have left. The most insolent of enemies is one who is insolent towards Allah in His sanctuary, or kills one other than his killer, or kills by entering the Jāhiliyya.» [Translator's note: so printed; the last phrase is known in the ḥadīth as «or kills for the blood-feuds of the Jāhiliyya» (bi-dhuḥūl al-jāhiliyya).] (أَفَمَنْ كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ) Resumptive speech, introduced to begin explaining the state of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers. The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied element required by the context, the implied form being "Is the matter not as mentioned? So is one who stands firm on a clear proof and evidence like one to whom [the evil of his deeds] has been made attractive?" (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", referring to (من); (على بيّنة) is the khabar; (من ربه) is an adjective of (بينة); (كمن) is the khabar [of من]; the clause (زين), in the passive, is the ṣila; (له) are attached to (زين); (سوء عمله) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (اتبعوا) is conjoined to (زين), and in it the meaning of (من) is observed, just as its wording was observed in (زين); and (أهواءهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ فِيها أَنْهارٌ مِنْ ماءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ لَذَّةٍ لِلشَّارِبِينَ) (مثل الجنة) is a mubtadaʾ — the discussion of its khabar will come; (التي) is an adjective, and the clause (وعد المتقون) is the ṣila. (فيها) is a fronted khabar and (أنهار) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الجنة), or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it — in it are rivers", or it falls within the domain of the ṣila as a repetition of it. (من ماء) is an adjective of (أنهار), and (غير آسن) a second adjective of (أنهار); (أنهار) is conjoined to the first (أنهار); (من خمر) is a naʿt, and (لذة للشاربين) a second naʿt; (للشاربين) are attached to (لذة) because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of taking pleasure, and it occurs as an adjective of the wine. It may also be the feminine of ladhdh, ladhdh meaning ladhīdh (delicious); on the first view it must be interpreted as a derived word so that it can validly serve as an adjective, in the manner of "Zayd is justice" meaning "just". More discussion of (لذة للشاربين) will come in the section on Benefits. [Translator's note: the Benefits section below does not in fact discuss (لذة للشاربين).] (وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى وَلَهُمْ فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) (أنهار) is conjoined to the preceding (أنهار); (من عسل) is an adjective, and (مصفّى) is an adjective of (عسل). The wāw is a conjunction; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) are attached to what the khabar is attached to, namely the omitted [notion of] being established; the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "kinds"; and (من كل الثمرات) is a naʿt of the omitted mubtadaʾ. (مغفرة) is conjoined to "kinds", or it is a mubtadaʾ whose fronted khabar is omitted, i.e. "and they have forgiveness"; and (من ربهم) is a naʿt of (مغفرة). (كَمَنْ هُوَ خالِدٌ فِي النَّارِ وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيماً فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعاءَهُمْ) (كمن) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "Is one who abides eternally in this Garden, according to what the promise stated, like one who abides eternally in the Fire?" On this view the khabar of (مثل) is implied: Sībawayh supplied it as "among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden", with the clause after it also explaining the description; al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl supplied it as "the description of the Garden is what you hear", with the clause after it also explanatory.
