﴿التي أخرجتك أهلكناهم﴾: «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قريتك»; the clause «أخرجتك» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «التي», with no grammatical position. The clause «أهلكناهم» is the khabar of «كأين».
﴿فلا ناصر لهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لا» is the lā of generic negation; «ناصر» is its noun, and «لهم» is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿أفمن كان على بينة﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted and implied, required by the context; «من» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject); «كان» is a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), referring to «من»; and «على بينة» is the khabar (predicate).
[Translator's note: «من» here is usually parsed as a relative noun, the interrogative force coming from the hamza; translated as written.]
﴿من ربه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «بينة»; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿كمن زين له﴾: «كمن»: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative, khabar; «من» is a relative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «زُيِّنَ», read as passive (constructed for one whose agent is not named), is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «زين».
﴿سوء عمله﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿واتبعوا﴾: conjoined to «زين».
﴿أهواءهم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
الَّذِينَ is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); it is an incomplete noun [i.e. it needs a ṣila (relative clause)]. كَفَرُوا is part of its ṣila, and «وصدّوا» is conjoined to it.
وَصَدُّوا is written with an extra alif after the wāw, and the grammarians have three views on this. The doctrine of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, is that this alif was added in writing to distinguish between the wāw of the pronoun and an original wāw, as in «لو»; the alif was chosen because it is at the end of the place of articulation of the wāw. Al-Akhfash said: if it were written without alif, it would be read «كفر وصدّ», so it distinguishes between this wāw and the wāw of conjunction. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: it was written with alif to distinguish between the attached and the detached pronoun: one writes «صدّوهم عن المسجد الحرام» without alif, and writes «صدّوا هم» with alif, as you say "qāmū hum".
Abū Jaʿfar said: These are three views, the soundest of which is the first, because al-Akhfash's view is countered by the fact that one may say "kafara wa-afʿalu" (he disbelieved, and I do …), so the confusion arises again; and Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā's statement about the distinction makes it only between the two pronouns, while in قاموا no accusative pronoun occurs, so on his view he would be obliged to write it without alif — and neither he nor anyone else does that. The doctrine of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, is a sound doctrine. This applies to the wāw of the plural specifically. As for the one in the singular, as in your saying "huwa yarjū", it is without alif, because it is not the wāw of the pronoun but the final radical of the verb, in the same status as the wāw of «لو»; writing it with alif is a mistake, even though one of the later scholars mentioned it without investigation. I saw Abū Isḥāq mention him as deficient in grammar, and he mentioned that he had addressed him about it.
Some of the Arabs say «اللّذون», making it a sound plural.
As for what Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ — that they are the disbelievers of the people of Mecca — he made the verse specific to them, while the apparent sense indicates generality; so it may have been revealed about particular people and then become general for everyone who does what they did. Likewise وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ: Ibn ʿAbbās's statement that this was revealed about the Anṣār specifically is in the same status as what preceded. «والذين» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar (predicate) is كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ. Mujāhid said from Ibn ʿAbbās: i.e. their affair; al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from him: i.e. their condition (shaʾn). Abū Jaʿfar said: al-bāl in the language is expressed by "affair", "condition" and "state". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-bāl may have another usage, in the meaning of the heart; one says "this does not occur to my bāl", i.e. to my heart.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ذلِكَ is in the position of a nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that"; it may also be in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, with what follows it as its khabar (predicate). ذلك then points to the leading astray and the guidance. The Arabs may point to two things with ذلك, and some of them say ذانك. I heard Abū Isḥāq say, concerning Sībawayh's statement "ẓanantu" without extending it to another object: ذلك points to two things — as if someone said "ẓanantu Zaydan munṭaliqan" (I thought Zayd was leaving), and another said to him "qad ẓanantu dhālika" (I thought that too).

nahhas-irab:4-6.t:
فَإِذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "strike the necks a striking". It is also said to be by way of incitement (al-ighrāʾ); this is al-Farrāʾ's view. حَتَّى إِذا أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ فَشُدُّوا الْوَثاقَ, i.e. lest they flee or some harm reach you from them. al-ithkhān is excess in striking, derived from their saying "a thick (thakhīn) thing", i.e. dense.
فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِداءً: two maṣdars; the verb was omitted because the maṣdar indicates it and because it is a command. al-fidāʾ may be lengthened or shortened according to the Basrans. As for al-Farrāʾ, he reported that it is lengthened when its first letter has kasra and shortened when its first letter has fatḥa, and he reported: "qum fadan laka" (rise, may I be your ransom).
حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها: the people of exegesis hold that the meaning is "until polytheism ceases". The pronoun, according to al-Farrāʾ, bears two meanings: one is "until the war lays down their burdens", i.e. their sins; the other is that it refers back to the war itself. Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ḥarb in the speech of the Arabs is feminine, and they form its diminutive without hāʾ, saying ḥurayb; and like it are qaws (bow) and dhawd (small herd of camels), whose diminutives are formed without hāʾ, as heard from the Arabs.
ذلِكَ وَلَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَانْتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ: «ذلك» is in the position of a nominative, i.e. "the matter is that: that if Allah willed He would take vengeance on them" — but He willed to reward the believers, and the wisdom in that was that reward and punishment might take place. He, Mighty and Majestic, made that clear by His saying: وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَا بَعْضَكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ.
وَالَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ: this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read وَالَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ; Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿraj read قُتِلُوا; and from al-Ḥasan it is reported that he read «قتّلوا» with doubling. [Translator's note: the readings are printed indistinguishably in the source. The reading of the first group is «قاتَلُوا»; that of Abū ʿAmr (and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim) is «قُتِلُوا»; al-Jaḥdarī's is reported as «قَتَلُوا»; al-Ḥasan's is «قُتِّلُوا».] Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading has the authority of the community, and it is clearer in meaning. Some of the linguists claimed that he chooses to read «قاتلوا», because if one reads «قُتلوا» the reward is only for whoever was killed, and if one reads «قُتلوا» the reward is only for whoever was killed, whereas if one reads «قاتلوا» the reward covers the whole group. [Translator's note: the clause about «قتلوا» is repeated in the source.] This, by my life, is a good argument, except that the people of reasoning say: when a word (ḥarf) is read in several ways, it is in the status of [separate] verses, each one conveying a meaning; and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been given comprehensive speech (jawāmiʿ al-kalim)."

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَنْصُرُوا اللَّهَ يَنْصُرْكُمْ: it is said the meaning is "if you support the religion of Allah and His allies", and that was made a support of Him figuratively; يَنْصُرْكُمْ in the Hereafter, i.e. He will ward off hardships from you. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: He will give you victory over your enemy. وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَكُمْ: it is said: at the place of reckoning, by making the proof in your favour.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); it may also be in the position of an accusative by an implied verb which فَتَعْساً لَهُمْ explains. وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ is conjoined to the omitted verb.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Abū Isḥāq said: They disliked the sending down of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا: [فينظروا] is in the position of an accusative as an answer (jawāb); it may also be in the position of a jussive as conjoined; the sign of both jussive and accusative is the dropping of the nūn. كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ: [عاقبة is] the noun of كان; He did not say «كانت» because it is a non-real feminine; the khabar (predicate) of «كان» is in «كيف». وَلِلْكافِرِينَ أَمْثالُها: al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: a punishment that will come down from the sky and has not yet happened. Abū Isḥāq said about the pronoun in أمثالها that it refers back to the outcome (al-ʿāqiba).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا — he said: their Helper. Al-Farrāʾ said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ذلك بأنّ الله وليّ الذين آمنوا», and this is a reading by way of explanation (tafsīr). Abū Isḥāq said about its meaning: that Allah takes charge of those who believe in all their affairs, their guidance and victory over their enemy. These views are close to one another, and it is known in the language that al-mawlā is al-walī; that is the meaning of what Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-mawlā is the helper. On this basis is interpreted the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever I am his mawlā, ʿAlī is his mawlā", i.e. whoever I befriend and help, ʿAlī befriends and helps him. It has also been said that the meaning is: whoever befriends me and helps me, let him befriend ʿAlī and help him.
That is made clear by what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān narrated to us from Abū Saʿīd al-Sukkarī, from Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn al-Mustanīr [Quṭrub], who said: If someone asks about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الْكافِرِينَ لا مَوْلى لَهُمْ (11) and says: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the mawlā of everyone, so how did He, Mighty and Majestic, say "and that the disbelievers have no mawlā"? — the answer is that al-mawlā here is al-walī (protecting friend), and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not the walī of the disbelievers. And he recited [metre: al-kāmil]:
426- فغدت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنّه ... مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها
(So she set off, reckoning that each of the two openings, behind her and before her, was the [proper] place (mawlā) of danger.)
i.e. the walī of danger.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَالنَّارُ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مثوى» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ allowed مَثْوىً to be in the position of an accusative, with the khabar being لهم.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: The implied form is "and how many of the people of a town" [Translator's note: on وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ]. It is أيّ, which the kāf of comparison has entered. Al-Farrāʾ said about the meaning of «التي أخرجتك»: [the town] whose people drove you out — to Medina. أَهْلَكْناهُمْ فَلا ناصِرَ لَهُمْ: al-Farrāʾ said: it came in the exegesis [that the meaning is]: they had no helper until We destroyed them. He said: so «فلا ناصر لهم» would be [meaning] today, from the punishment.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَفَمَنْ كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ is according to the wording [of من]; if it were according to the meaning it would be said «كانوا على بيّنة من ربهم». Likewise كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ, and He did not say «لهم سوء أعمالهم». After it, وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ is according to the meaning; if it were according to the wording it would be «واتّبع هواه».

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ: there are four views on its meaning. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Sībawayh said: i.e. "among what is recited to you and narrated to you is the description (mathal) of the Garden". Yūnus said: mathal means "description" (ṣifa), and its like, as we have mentioned, is مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمالُهُمْ كَرَمادٍ [Ibrāhīm: 18]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Both views are good and fine. Al-Kisāʾī said: the likeness of the Garden is such-and-such, and in it is such-and-such, and they have in it such-and-such, كَمَنْ هُوَ خالِدٌ فِي النَّارِ, i.e. the likeness of these in good is like the likeness of those in evil, i.e. these are like those.
The fourth view is from Abū Isḥāq, who said: مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ is an explanation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ [al-Ḥajj: 14]; then He explained those rivers. So the meaning is: the likeness of the Garden promised to the God-fearing, from what you have known in this world of gardens and rivers, is a garden فِيها أَنْهارٌ مِنْ ماءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ.
In the reading of the people of Mecca, according to what Abū Ḥātim mentioned, it is «غَيْرِ أَسِنٍ» on the pattern faʿil [Translator's note: the source prints the Meccan form identically to the received «آسِنٍ»]. One says asana al-māʾu yaʾsinu and yaʾsunu asnan and usūnan, so it is āsin; and asina yaʾsanu asanan, so it is asin — and the kasra may be dropped for its heaviness, so one says asn — when it stinks. If it [merely] changes, they say ajana al-māʾu yaʾjinu and yaʾjunu.
وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ لَذَّةٍ لِلشَّارِبِينَ: [لذّة is] a naʿt (adjective) of خمر in the meaning "possessing delight"; لذّة may also be a naʿt of أنهار; and the accusative is also permissible as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say "huwa laka hibatan" (it is yours as a gift).
كَمَنْ هُوَ خالِدٌ فِي النَّارِ: the kāf is in the position of a nominative, and it stands in mutual nominative relation (murāfiʿa) with مثل according to al-Kisāʾī, as we explained. As for al-Farrāʾ, the implied form according to him is: "Is one who is in these gardens like one who abides eternally in the Fire?"
وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيماً فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعاءَهُمْ: plural of miʿan, which is masculine and feminine. Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī narrated from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيماً فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعاءَهُمْ, that he said: "When it is brought near him he finds it loathsome, and when it is brought close to him it scorches his face and the skin of his scalp and the flesh of his face fall into it; and when he drinks it, it cuts his bowels and comes out from his rear."

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ is according to the wording of «من». حَتَّى إِذا خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ is according to the meaning. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda said: they said that to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ is also according to the meaning.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا, i.e. accepted guidance and acted upon it. زادَهُمْ هُدىً: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it. Among the good things said about the pronoun is that the meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, increased them in guidance by what He sends down of verses, proofs, indications and arguments to His Messenger ﷺ, so that the believers increase thereby in insight and knowledge.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً: this is the reading on which rests the authority of the community. Abū ʿUbayd reported that in some of the codices of the Kufans it is «إن تأتهم». [Translator's note: the source prints «أن تأتيهم» here, but the continuation shows that the codex form meant is «إن تأتهم».] It was read out to Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī narrated to me, saying: I said to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: What is this fāʾ in His saying فَقَدْ جاءَ أَشْراطُها? He said: It is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition. I said: But it is أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ. He said: God forbid! It is only «إن تأتهم». Al-Farrāʾ said: I thought he took it from the people of Mecca, because he read [the Qur'an] with them. He said: and it is in some of the codices of the Kufans «إن تأتهم» with a single tooth [i.e. with one letter-stroke for the yāʾ], but none of them read it so. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not known from Abū ʿAmr except by this route; what is known from him is that he read «أن تأتيهم». And that [reading], besides its irregularity, contradicts the text of the codex (al-sawād) and departs from the authority of the community. [Translator's note: the source has «وتلك ال مع شذوذها», with a word evidently missing after «ال», probably «القراءة».] From the side of meaning there is more: if it were «إن تأتهم بغتة», the meaning would be that it might come suddenly or not suddenly, whereas Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: لا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلَّا بَغْتَةً [al-Aʿrāf: 187].
فَقَدْ جاءَ أَشْراطُها: plural of sharaṭ, i.e. its signs. Al-Ḥasan said: the death of the Prophet ﷺ is among its signs. Others said: the sending of the Prophet ﷺ is among its signs, because there is no prophet after him until the Hour arrives; and he, upon him be peace, said: "I and the Hour are like these two." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: it was said sharaṭ (shuraṭ) only because they have signs and appearances that the common people do not have. [Translator's note: the reference is apparently to the shurṭa (police), named from their distinguishing marks.]
فَأَنَّى لَهُمْ إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْراهُمْ: al-Akhfash said: i.e. how will they have their reminder when the Hour comes to them? «ذكراهم» is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the doctrine of Sībawayh, and by the adverbial (al-ṣifa) [i.e. the preposition phrase] according to the view of the Kufans.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t:
فَاعْلَمْ: Abū Isḥāq said: the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of a condition, i.e. We have made clear that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is One, so know that. As for addressing the Prophet ﷺ with this while he knows it, there is more than one answer to that. Abū Isḥāq said: addressing the Prophet ﷺ is addressing his community. According to the doctrine of some grammarians, the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to address others with this, like فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ [Yūnus: 94]. It is also said: know with knowledge additional to your knowledge, because a person may know a thing from several aspects. A fourth answer is that the meaning is a warning to him against acts of disobedience, i.e. know that there is no god but Allah alone, and none other than He punishes for disobedience; what indicates this is that after it comes وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ, just as you say to a man, warning him against disobedience, "Know that you will die": you are not commanding him to perform the act of knowing, but only warning him against disobedience.
Abū Isḥāq said: وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ, i.e. your going about, وَمَثْواكُمْ, i.e. your abode in this world and the Hereafter. He said: وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا الْقِتالُ, i.e. it was made obligatory. فَأَوْلى لَهُمْ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ: there are several answers about it. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh gave two answers. One is that طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ are nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "obedience and a fitting word are better"; the second is as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our affair is obedience and a fitting word". Others said: the implied form is "from us is obedience". A fourth view is that «طاعة» is a naʿt (adjective) of سورة in the meaning "possessing [a command of] obedience".
فَإِذا عَزَمَ الْأَمْرُ, i.e. the matter became serious. It is also said: it is figurative, i.e. the people in charge of the matter, i.e. when the Prophet ﷺ resolved on war. فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا اللَّهَ in fighting, لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ than making excuses and fleeing. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. their being true to Allah and their faith in Him would have been better for them.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ: this is the reading on which the community is agreed. Abū Isḥāq said: if «عَسِيتم» were permissible, «عَسِيَ ربُّكم» would be permissible; so according to him it is not permissible at all. [Translator's note: the source prints «عسيتم» unvocalized; the form under discussion is «عَسِيتُم» with kasra, the reading of Nāfiʿ.] It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read «إن تُوُلِّيتُم», i.e. "if people are put in charge of you", in the passive. [Translator's note: printed identically to the received text in the source; the passive form is implied by the explanation.] أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ: (أن) is in the position of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of عسيتم. This is the eloquent usage; some of the Arabs omit «أن» from the khabar, as [the poet] said [metre: al-wāfir]:
427- عسى الهمّ الّذي أمسيت فيه ... يكون وراءه فرج قريب
(Perhaps the worry in which I find myself will have, behind it, a near relief.)
And some of the Arabs bring a noun as its khabar and put it in the accusative, saying "ʿasā Zaydun qāʾiman" (perhaps Zayd will be standing).

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وَأَعْمى أَبْصارَهُمْ (23) — then He, Mighty and Majestic, said after it أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ, although their description with deafness and blindness has come before. Among the soundest and best things said about this is that the meaning is: those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He did not grant them reward, and they are in the status of the deaf who do not hear good praise of themselves and do not see the reward that would gladden them. This is a clear answer. It has also been said that it is an imprecation; and it has been said that "they do not hear" means "they do not know".
Some scholars interpreted the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, "The dead person hears the tread of their sandals", as "knows"; and [likewise] the interpretation of the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ about the people of the well who were killed on the day of Badr, when he addressed them, saying, "Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?", and then informed that they hear that: the author of that interpretation interpreted it as meaning that they know it, and argued from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى [al-Naml: 80]. A group of scholars rejected this interpretation against those who held it, because the Prophet ﷺ is the one who explains on behalf of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; he is the one who said, "The dead person hears the tread of their sandals", and who told of the punishment of the grave and the questioning of the dead; and likewise most of his Companions, on that basis, report that [the reward of] deeds reaches the dead. The correct thing on this is to say: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, conveys to the dead of the children of Adam what He wills, as He wills, and punishes whom He wills of those who deserve it, with what He wills. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic, وَما أَنْتَ بِمُسْمِعٍ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ [Fāṭir: 22] and إِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى [al-Naml: 80], there is no contradiction of this in them. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is only: you do not make the dead hear by your own power or strength, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes them hear as He wills. What indicates this is that after it comes وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ [al-Naml: 81], i.e. you do not guide them by your own power, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guides whom He wills by His kindness and grant of success.
أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفالُها (24): أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ, i.e. so that they act upon what is in it and come to know its indications; أَمْ عَلى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفالُها, i.e. locks that prevent them from that.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. they returned to disbelief after hearing guidance and having it made clear. الشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ وَأَمْلى لَهُمْ: this is the reading of most of the imams. Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿraj, Shayba and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «وأُمْلِيَ لهم» in the passive; Mujāhid, Sallām and Yaʿqūb read «وأُمْلِي لهم» with the yāʾ made quiescent. [Translator's note: the source prints both variants unvocalized; the vocalization follows the descriptions given.] The first reading means "and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted them respite"; the second reading comes back to this meaning, because it is known that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the one who granted them respite; and the third reading is clear: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informs that He grants them respite. The Kufans pronounce وَأَمْلى لَهُمْ with imāla (inclination of the vowel), because the alif is converted from a yāʾ. The meaning of amlā lahu is: He prolonged his life and did not hasten his punishment; it is derived from al-malāwa, which is a stretch of time; from it comes "mallāka Allāh, Mighty and Majestic, niʿmatahu" (may Allah let you enjoy His blessing for long), "tamalla ḥabībaka" (enjoy your beloved for long), and al-malawān: night and day.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُوا ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. the matter is that leading astray, for they said to the Jews: "We will obey you in part of the matter", i.e. in cooperating in enmity towards Muḥammad ﷺ. وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِسْرارَهُمْ: this is the reading of most of the imams; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «والله يعلم إسرارهم», and this is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of asarra, while the first is the plural of sirr. [Translator's note: the source vocalizes the first reading as إِسْرارَهُمْ and prints the second unvocalized; per the explanation, the reading of most imams is «أَسْرارَهُم» (plural of sirr) and that of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is «إِسْرارَهُم» (maṣdar).]

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: فَكَيْفَ إِذا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ: there is an omission in it, i.e. "so how will their state be?" يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبارَهُمْ: Mujāhid said: i.e. their buttocks; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is noble and uses allusion.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أَسْخَطَ اللَّهَ, i.e. that is their recompense, because they followed the thing [that] angered Allah — abandoning following the Prophet ﷺ. وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ, i.e. following His law and believing in Him. فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ, i.e. so that nullified [their deeds]; the meaning may also be: so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nullified whatever good they did, because of their disbelief.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ: from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they are the hypocrites. He said: and the sickness is doubt and denial. أَنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغانَهُمْ: he said: their enmity towards the believers. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-ḍighn is the ill will that you harbour; and one says ḍaghintu ʿalayhi and iḍṭaghantu.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَأَرَيْناكَهُمْ فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ بِسِيماهُمْ: in the same meaning one also says sīmiyāʾ. وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِي لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ: from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Prophet ﷺ never saw a hypocrite and addressed him without recognizing him. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: فِي لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ means in its drift and in its intent, without explicit statement; he said: and close to its meaning is al-taʿrīḍ (allusion). In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps one of you is more alḥan in his argument than the other, so I judge in his favour according to what I hear; whoever I judge to have something of his brother's right, I am only cutting off for him a piece of the Fire." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the meaning of «ألحن بحجّته» is more pointed and more effective in it. He said: and from it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to the two Saʿds when he sent them to the Banū Qurayẓa: "If you find them keeping the covenant, announce that openly; and if you find them otherwise, convey it to me in an allusion (laḥn) that I will recognize, and do not weaken the resolve of the Muslims."

nahhas-irab:31-33.t: al-ibtilāʾ in the language is testing. It is said the meaning is: We shall certainly make the duties of worship severe for you — that is, in the command to strive (jihād) and the prohibition of acts of disobedience; what indicates that is حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ الْمُجاهِدِينَ مِنْكُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ. وَنَبْلُوَا أَخْبارَكُمْ, i.e. what you did in what you were charged with as worship.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: The fāʾ entered the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» because its noun is الذين and its ṣila (relative clause) is a verb, so it resembled a conditional and the fāʾ entered it. If you said "inna Zaydan fa-munṭaliqun", it would not be permissible.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
فَلا تَهِنُوا: the original is «توهنوا»; the wāw was dropped following [the pattern of the imperfect, as in yaʿidu]. وَتَدْعُوا is conjoined to it; it may also be an answer (jawāb) [i.e. accusative after the wāw of accompaniment]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-salm, al-silm and al-musālama are one. وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ: Mujāhid said: the victors. وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ, i.e. He will help you. وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمالَكُمْ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. He will not wrong you; Abū Isḥāq took it as involving an omission, i.e. He will not diminish for you the reward of your deeds.
Yūnus narrated from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father — and ʿAnbasa says: from ʿUmar — from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever misses the ʿaṣr prayer, it is as if he has been deprived (wutira) of his family and his wealth", i.e. diminished and despoiled. Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two views on its derivation. Al-Farrāʾ's doctrine is that it is derived from al-watr, which is blood-vengeance (al-dhaḥl): killing a man and taking his wealth; so the one who misses the ʿaṣr prayer, because of the reward and recompense he has missed, is in the status of one whose family and wealth have been taken, i.e. he is in the status of one who has suffered watr. The other derivation is that it is from al-witr, which is the single, as though he were in the status of one who has been left alone. It [the ʿaṣr prayer] was singled out for this because it falls at the time of their occupations and livelihoods. The original of يتركم is «يوتركم». [The preposition] was dropped [so that it took] two objects, like وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا [al-Aʿrāf: 155]; the implied form according to al-Akhfash is "He will not deprive you in your deeds".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: إِنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا: Abū Isḥāq said: He has made known to them that their reward is the Garden. He said: and وَلا يَسْئَلْكُمْ أَمْوالَكُمْ [with the nominative] is permissible — he means by making it a statement — and the jussive is by conjunction. It is said the meaning is: He does not command you to spend all your wealth on striving and on comforting the poor.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: فَيُحْفِكُمْ تَبْخَلُوا, i.e. you withhold what is due from you. Abū Jaʿfar said: and such is bukhl (miserliness) in the language. وَيُخْرِجْ أَضْغانَكُمْ: it is said: i.e. that miserliness would bring out your rancour, i.e. what you harbour of refusing to spend, for fear of poverty.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وَمَنْ يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّما: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb). فَإِنَّما يَبْخَلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ, i.e. the harm and the punishment return only upon him. وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ, i.e. so He did not charge you with that, because of what He knew of you. وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ: it is said: if you turn away from supporting the Prophet ﷺ, He will bring other people in your place, ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أَمْثالَكُمْ in what you did.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.
Abū Yaḥyā related from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: he said: the people of Mecca.
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ﴾: he said: the Anṣār.
﴿وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ﴾: he said: their affair.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ is: He nullified them, as the Exalted said ﴿وَقَالُوا أَئِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الأَرْضِ﴾; and the meaning is: We did not reward them for what they did, because of their disbelief.
And the meaning of ﴿كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ﴾ is: He covered them over, and did not hold them to account for what they did in the time of their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿دَمَّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ أَمْثَالُهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: And for the disbelievers is destruction, as a threat from Allah.
And someone else said: So those of them who were killed were killed by the sword.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَأَنَّ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ لاَ مَوْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the protecting ally (walī) of those who believe.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is likewise. And the poet said:
فَغَدَتْ كِلاَ الفَرْجَيْنِ تَحْسِبُ أَنَّهُ * مَوْلَى المَخَافَةِ خَلْفُهَا وَأَمَامُهَا
(So she set off at dawn, reckoning each of the two openings, behind her and before her, to be the "mawlā" of fear.)
That is, the walī (most fitting place) of fear.
And Simāk related from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: he said: They have no mawlā other than Him.
Qatāda said: This verse was revealed on the day of Uḥud, while the Prophet ﷺ was in the mountain pass, and the Muslims had been heavily stricken with killing and wounds. The idolaters shouted: A day for the day of Badr! We have al-ʿUzzā and you have no ʿUzzā! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿والَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوْلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَأَنَّ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ لاَ مَوْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
So the Prophet ﷺ said to them [the Muslims]: Say: "Allah is our Mawlā and you have no mawlā; our slain are alive, provided for in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire."
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: Allah is the protecting ally of those who believe in guidance and help.
So when He had told of His alliance with the believers and His abandonment of the disbelievers, He made known what He has prepared for the believers and the disbelievers, saying: ﴿إنَّ اللهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا
الصَّالِحَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الأَنْهَارُ﴾, i.e. an abode for them.
﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَمَا تَأْكُلُ ٱلأَنْعَامُ وَٱلنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِّن قَرْيَتِكَ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ فَلاَ نَاصِرَ لَهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means the people of Mecca. He said: so they have no helper.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He is Muḥammad ﷺ.
﴿كَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوۤءُ عَمَلِهِ﴾: he said: They are the idolaters of the Arabs.
Then He said ﴿وَٱتَّبَعُوۤاْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ [in the plural], according to the meaning of "man" (whoever) [rather than its singular form].

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ فِيهَآ أَنْهَارٌ مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ﴾.
And He did not bring the thing likened to it.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- Among them: that mathal has the meaning of "description" (ṣifa); al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl and al-Farrāʾ said that.
And it is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, that he read ﴿أَمْثَالُ
الجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So this is one view; and according to it "mathal" has the sense of "mithl", and there is in it a difference from its meaning, just as in "ʿidl" there is a difference from the meaning of "ʿadl".
b- And it is said the meaning is: The likeness of the Garden that the God-fearing have been promised, in terms of what you know in this world, is a garden in which there are rivers.
c- And the third view: that the meaning is by way of rebuke and making [them] acknowledge, i.e. is the likeness of the Garden that the God-fearing have been promised like one who abides forever in the Fire? That is, is the likeness of the obedient one in your view like the likeness of the disobedient one?
And Maʿmar related from Qatāda: ﴿مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ﴾: he said: not putrid.
Qatāda said: al-āsin is the altered, the stagnant (al-ājin).
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's [first] statement is sounder, because one says asana al-māʾu, yaʾsanu and yaʾsunu, so it is āsin and asin, when it stinks so that no one can drink it; and ajina, yaʾjanu, so it is ājin, when it has altered, even if it is drunk reluctantly.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِّنْ خَمْرٍ لَّذَّةٍ لِّلشَّارِبِينَ﴾.
One says: sharābun ladhīdh and ladhdh (a delicious drink).
﴿وَأَنْهَارٌ مِّنْ عَسَلٍ مُّصَفًّى﴾: that is, not like the honey of this world, which contains wax and other things.
﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَاتِ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ﴾: that is, and they have forgiveness from their Lord.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿كَمَنْ هُوَ خَالِدٌ فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The discussion of it has preceded.
And there is another view on it, namely that the meaning is: Is one who will abide forever in the Garden, and in this bliss mentioned, like one who abides forever in the Fire? Then this was omitted because the listener knows it, as the Exalted said ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجِداً
وَقَائِماً﴾ — even though it has been said that the meaning [there] is: O you who are devoutly obedient.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are the hypocrites.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا خَرَجُواْ مِنْ عِندِكَ قَالُواْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ مَاذَا قَالَ آنِفاً﴾.
That is, when they heard the Prophet ﷺ preaching, then went out, they said to the Muslims mockingly: ﴿مَاذَا قَالَ آنِفاً﴾? That is, we paid no attention to what he said.
And the meaning is: What did he say just now, i.e. at the time closest to us? From their saying: istaʾnaftu al-shayʾa (I began the thing anew), and rawḍatun unuf: a meadow not yet grazed.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَوْاْ زَادَهُمْ هُدًى وَآتَاهُمْ تَقُوَاهُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: Allah increased them in guidance; so the pronoun refers back to His saying ﴿أُوْلَئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and the speech of the Prophet increased them in guidance.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and the mockery of the hypocrites increased them in guidance.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَآتَاهُمْ تَقُوَاهُمْ﴾: that is, He inspired them [with it].
And it is possible that the meaning is: the reward of their piety.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: thus Allah makes clear the matter of good deeds and evil deeds.
And the meaning of "ḍarabtu lahu mathalan" (I struck him a likeness) is: I made clear to him a kind (ḍarb) of likenesses, i.e. a type of them.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَضَرْبَ ٱلرِّقَابِ﴾.
That is, then kill them; and the necks are mentioned because killing most often happens by [striking] them.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْ فَشُدُّواْ ٱلْوَثَاقَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Taking captives should not happen until the enemy has been heavily subdued by killing, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ
أَسْرَى حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الأَرْضِ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإمَّا مَنًّا وإمَّا فَدَاءً حَتَّى تَضَعَ الحَرْبُ
أَوْزَارَهَا﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is disagreement about this verse.
Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAṭāʾ disliked the killing of a captive in cold blood (ṣabran), because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً﴾; and he said: Release [him] as a favour or ransom [him], but do not kill.
And Qatāda said: The verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِمَّا
تَثْقَفَنَّهم في الحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾.
And Shuʿba related from al-Ḥakam, who said: Mughīra asked me about an obscure abrogated verse, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً﴾.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is abrogating; it abrogated His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا
المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is clear about the verse is that it is neither abrogated nor abrogating; rather this is a permission, and likewise killing [is permitted], because the Prophet ﷺ killed and ransomed. And He mentioned killing in another verse, namely ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ
وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾, and so sufficed with that.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, until the people of shirk embrace Islam; so He called them "war" (ḥarb).
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلْحَرْبُ أَوْزَارَهَا﴾: Until Jesus son of Mary descends, breaks the cross and kills the swine, and the religions vanish except the religion of Islam, and the creed becomes one.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So this is one view on the verse, i.e. until the people of war lay down their burdens, and so embrace Islam or make peace.
And it is said: by al-awzār here the weapons are meant, as the poet said:
وَأَعْدَدْتُ لِلْحَرْبِ أَوْزَارَهَا * رِمَاحاً طِوَالاً، وخَيْلاً ذُكُوراً
(And I prepared for war its "burdens": long spears and stallion horses.)
And the meaning according to this is: then bind fast the fetters until the war lays down its burdens, then either a favour afterwards or a ransom.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَاْ بَعْضَكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.
That is, to purify the believers and to obliterate the disbelievers.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَن يُضِلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.
And it is read ﴿قَتَلُوا﴾, ﴿قُتِّلُوا﴾ and ﴿قُتِلُوا﴾.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَيَهْدِيهِمْ وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَهُمْ وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَهَا لَهُمْ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
Mujāhid said: He acquainted them with its houses and dwellings and allotted them their shares of it, so that none of them errs and enters a place other than his own, nor needs to seek directions.
And Salama ibn Kuhayl said: ﴿عَرَّفَهَا لَهُمْ﴾: He acquainted them with its paths. So this is one view.
And it is said: ﴿عَرَّفَهَا﴾: He made it fragrant.
And it is said: ﴿عَرَّفَهَا﴾: He raised it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view — even though some lexicographers have rejected it, saying: if it were so, He would have said "ʿarrafahum bihā" (He acquainted them with it) — is the best and soundest of the views, and this rebuttal is not binding.
And the meaning is: He made it clear to them, so they recognised it clearly.
The second view is not impossible, because one says ṭaʿāmun muʿarraf, i.e. perfumed.
And the third view is taken from al-ʿurf (the crest), because of its elevation.
And it is said: that is, He made known to the morally responsible among His servants that it is for them.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَتَعْساً لَّهُمْ وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.
That is, [they are] among those of whom it should be said: May Allah make them fall (atʿasahumu Allāh), i.e. may He not restore them; and this is invoked against one who stumbles.
And Thaʿlab said: al-taʿs is evil. He said: And it is said: it is remoteness; and intakasa: his affair was overturned and ruined.
And Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-taʿs is to fall headlong on one's head. He said: and al-taʿs is also destruction. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads البن السكيت, a misprint for ابن السكيت, Ibn al-Sikkīt.]»

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا﴾.
That is, are they waiting for anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly?
﴿فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, its signs; the singular is sharaṭ.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمْ إِذَا جَآءَتْهُمْ ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾? [Verse 18].
Qatāda said: That is, how can they then take heed?
Abū Jaʿfar said: So the meaning according to this is: whence will they have the benefit of remembrance, when the Hour has come and repentance has been cut off?

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنبِكَ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
And the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community.
That is, hold firm to this.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُّحْكَمَةٌ وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا ٱلْقِتَالُ﴾.
Qatāda said: Every sura in which fighting is mentioned is muḥkama (unabrogated).
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a difficult verse. And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَإذَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُحْدِثَةٌ﴾.
And the meaning is one, i.e. abrogation has not befallen it, and fighting is mentioned in it.
The Muslims only used to say this because they found comfort in the descent of revelation.
﴿رَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ﴾: that is, doubt and uncertainty. ﴿يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ نَظَرَ ٱلْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾: that is, the look of people enraged and distressed, as the Exalted said ﴿وَإنْ يَكَادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ
بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾. They only disliked the mention of fighting because, if they held back from it, their hypocrisy would become evident, so they feared being killed.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿فَأَوْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾, by way of threat.
Its literal sense is: the hateful thing has come near them, i.e. the hateful thing is closest to them. And the Arabs say to anyone who came close to destruction and then escaped: "awlā laka", i.e. you nearly perished.
As it is related that a Bedouin kept shooting at game, and it would escape him, and he would say: awlā laka (that was close for you). Then he shot at a game animal and came close to it, then it escaped him, and he said:
فَلَوْ كَانَ "أَوْلَى" يُطْعِمُ القَوْمَ صِدْتُهُمْ * وَلَكِنَّ "أَوْلَى" تَتْرُكُ النَّاسَ جُوَّعاً
(If "awlā" fed people, I would have hunted [enough] for them; but "awlā" leaves people hungry.)

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿طَاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ فَإِذَا عَزَمَ ٱلأَمْرُ فَلَوْ صَدَقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, obedience to Allah and speaking what is right in the realities of matters.
That is, hearing and obeying is better for them.
And al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: That is, obedience and a fitting word are more befitting [Translator's note: i.e. ṭāʿatun is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) "amthal" is omitted].
And there is another view on the meaning: namely that He related what they used to say before [the command to] fight was revealed, and before it was made obligatory.
So the meaning according to this is: they say: From us [there is] obedience and a fitting word.
And what indicates the soundness of this view is ﴿فَإِذَا عَزَمَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, the matter became serious.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So the implied meaning (taqdīr) according to this is: then when the matter became serious with the obligation of fighting, they disliked that — then this was omitted.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَوْ صَدَقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: So if they had been true to Allah in faith and in jihad.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَن تُفْسِدُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوۤاْ أَرْحَامَكُمْ﴾.
Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī said: These are the Ḥarūriyya.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: That is, would you perhaps, if you took charge of affairs, kill one another, as Quraysh killed Banū Hāshim and as Banū Hāshim killed Quraysh?
And there is another view on the meaning: namely, do you wish, if you turned away from the Prophet ﷺ and disbelieved in what he brought you, to go back to the disbelief you were in, and so spread corruption in the land through disbelief and sever your ties of kinship by burying your daughters alive?
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, read ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾, i.e. [if] you are placed under authority. «[Translator's note: the reading is printed here identical to the standard text; the gloss "if you are placed under authority" implies the passive variant تُوُلِّيتُمْ.]»

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱرْتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰ أَدْبَارِهِمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَى ٱلشَّيْطَانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ وَأَمْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: These are the People of the Book; they had the description of Muḥammad ﷺ, but they denied it and disbelieved, after guidance had become clear to them.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the people of hypocrisy.
﴿ٱلشَّيْطَانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ﴾: Qatāda said: that is, he made [it] seem fair to them.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَمْلَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: and Allah granted them respite, i.e. Allah extended their terms for them for a long span of time, as the Exalted said ﴿وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ إنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ﴾.
And Mujāhid read: ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ وأُمْلِي لَهُمْ﴾.
This is a good reading, and the meaning is: and I grant them respite.
And al-Farrāʾ reported that it was read ﴿وَأُمْلِيَ لَهُمْ﴾, and it is the reading of Shayba and Abū ʿAmr.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُواْ مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ سَنُطِيعُكُمْ فِي بَعْضِ ٱلأَمْرِ﴾.
[That is, in joining forces in enmity towards Muḥammad ﷺ].
And Sufyān said: He means the obligatory duties.
Qatāda said: They are the hypocrites.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَانَهُمْ﴾.
That is, their enmity... that is, [that He would make them] show their enmity towards the people of Islam.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لأَرَيْنَاكَهُمْ فَلَعَرَفْتَهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِي لَحْنِ ٱلْقَوْلِ﴾.
That is, We would have made them known to you; one says: araytuka kadhā, i.e. I made it known to you.
﴿فَلَعَرَفْتَهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ﴾: that is, by their mark.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِي لَحْنِ ٱلْقَوْلِ﴾.
That is, its import and its meaning, as the poet said:
مَنْطِقٌ صَائِبٌ وَتَلْحَنُ أَحْيَاناً * وَخَيْرُ الحَدِيثِ مَا كَانَ لَحْناً
(Speech that hits the mark, and at times you speak by allusion; and the best talk is that which is allusion.)
That is, what is not stated explicitly, and what is understood through the meaning and the drift of the speech.
And their saying "laḥana so-and-so in this" only means: he went off in a direction other than the correct one.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ وَلَن يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He will not diminish [anything of] you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: From this is the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever misses the ʿAṣr prayer, it is as though he had been bereft (wutira) of his family."

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن يَسْأَلْكُمُوهَا فَيُحْفِكُمْ تَبْخَلُواْ وَيُخْرِجْ أَضْغَانَكُمْ﴾.
﴿فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾: that is, He presses you hard; and from it is ḥafiyat al-dābba (the beast's hooves became worn out).
﴿وَيُخْرِجْ أَضْغَانَكُمْ﴾: it is said: that is, your enmity.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the rancour of your hearts, when you are asked for your wealth.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
«[Translator's note: this text, stored under 47:38, is the opening of the commentary on Sūrat al-Fatḥ (Sura 48).]»
Medinan in the narration of Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās.
And al-Zuhrī related from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwān, who both said: "Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed between Mecca and Medina, all of it concerning the affair of al-Ḥudaybiya."

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(عن سبيل) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (صدّوا), and the fāʿil (agent) of (أضلّ) is a pronoun referring to the Name of Majesty (الله). The clause «الذين كفروا ... أضلّ» has no grammatical position, being an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «صدّوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; and the clause «أضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).
2- The (الواو) is a conjunction in all three places. (بما) is attached to (آمنوا), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (على محمّد) is attached to (نزّل). The (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) - or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). (من ربّهم) is attached to an omitted word, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) «[Note: or it is attached to (بالحقّ).]». (عنهم) is attached to (كفّر) ...
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... كفّر عنهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the opening clause.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; the clause «آمنوا (الثانية)» (the second «آمنوا») has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause; the clause «نزّل ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما); the clause «هو الحقّ ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nāʾib fāʿil «[Note: or it has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.]»; the clause «كفّر عنهم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين آمنوا); and the clause «أصلح ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «كفّر».
3- (ذلك) is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ, in the position of nominative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الذين كفروا اتّبعوا) is in the position of genitive through the preposition «bāʾ», attached to an omitted word that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك); and the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الذين آمنوا اتّبعوا) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar. (من ربّهم) is attached to a ḥāl from (الحقّ). (كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing verb is (يضرب). (للناس) is attached to (يضرب) ..
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of what precedes; the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «اتّبعوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the first (أنّ); the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين) (the second); the clause «اتّبعوا الحقّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second (أنّ); and the clause «يضرب الله ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).

* Morphology:
(محمّد) is a proper noun derived from الحمد (praise), from the quadriliteral-form verb (حمّد); it is on the pattern of the passive participle, its wazn being مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the words of the Exalted «أَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ».
Here their deeds are likened to a stray camel that is neglected, having no master to guard it and care for its affairs; or he made them lost in their disbelief and sins and overwhelmed by them, as water is lost in milk.

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links what follows it to what precedes it by the tie of causation (al-sababiyya). (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to (ضرب) «[Note: it may be attached to the implied verb that governs (ضرب).]». (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ضرب) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, the maṣdar standing in for its verb in the imperative. (حتّى) is a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ). (إذا) is like the first, attached to (شدّوا). (الفاء) links the apodosis of the second condition. (الفاء) is a conjunction of ramification (li-l-tafrīʿ). (إمّا) is a particle of option (ḥarf takhyīr). (منا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e.: "either you show grace (tamunnū minnan) ..." and likewise (إمّا فداء). (بعد) is an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (منّا). (حتّى) is a particle of limit and of genitive. (تضع) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «an» after حتّى, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن تضع ... ) is in the position of genitive through (حتّى), attached to the content of the four events: the striking, the tightening of the bond, the showing of grace and the ransom. (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "The matter is that." (الواو) is a conjunction - or resumptive. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (اللام) links the apodosis of لو. (منهم) is attached to (انتصر), by including in it the meaning of "took revenge". (الواو) is a conjunction. (لكن) is for rectification (istidrāk) and has no governing effect. (اللام) is causal. (يبلو) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «an» after the lām, (ببعض) is attached to (يبلو), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلو ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He commanded you thus". (الواو) is resumptive, and the (الواو) in (قتلوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (في سبيل) is attached to (قتلوا). (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition ...
The clause «لقيتم ... » is in the position of genitive, by the annexation of إذا to it «[Note: the condition, its protasis and its apodosis follow upon the preceding rulings, i.e. if the matter is as mentioned of the misguidance of the disbelievers and the expiation of the evil deeds of the believers who do good ... then when you meet ..]». The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «(اضربوا) الرقاب ضربا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «أثخنتموهم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi «[Note: the wāw in (أثخنتموهم) is redundant; it is the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm.]». The clause «شدّوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «(تمنّون) منّا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis. The clause «(تفدون) فداء ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause (تمنون). The clause «تضع الحرب ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (the implied «an»).
The clause «(الأمر) ذلك ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical - or resumptive. The clause «لو يشاء الله ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumption that stands after حتّى the opening particle. The clause «انتصر منهم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause «(أمركم) ليبلو» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لو يشاء. The clause «يبلو ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (the implied «an»). The clause «الذين قتلوا ... لن يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «قتلوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «يضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين). The clause «سيهديهم ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The clause «يصلح ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause سيهديهم. 6- (الواو) is a conjunction. (الجنّة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension «[Note: the original is: He will admit them into the Garden.]». (لهم) is attached to (عرّفها). The clause «يدخلهم ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause سيهديهم. The clause «عرّفها ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: or it is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of يدخل or its object, with an implied «qad».]».

* Morphology:
(4) الوثاق: a noun for that with which captives are bound, namely the fetter or the rope; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fā', and its plural is وثق with two ḍammas. (فداء) is a samāʿī (heard, non-systematic) maṣdar of the triliteral verb فدى يفدي of the باب ضرب (pattern of ضرب). In the word there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) - or ibdāl (substitution): the weak letter, the yā', is turned into a hamza because it comes final after a silent alif; its origin is فداي ... And there are other maṣdars of the verb: فدى with fatḥa on the fā' and with kasra. (تضع) contains iʿlāl by deletion: it is a defective verb of the type mithāl (assimilated), its fā' being deleted in the imperfect, and its wazn is تعل with two fatḥas. (بعضكم) is a noun for a part or a portion or a group; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn, and its plural is أبعاض on the pattern أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
The mursal majāz (loose figurative usage): in the words of the Exalted «فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ».
It is a mursal majāz for killing, and killing is expressed by it to indicate that it ought to be by striking the neck wherever possible, and to depict it in the most dreadful image, because striking the neck involves making the head fly off, which is the noblest of the body's members and the seat of its senses, and the body is left cast down in a shocking posture - we seek refuge with Allah the Exalted. The relation (ʿalāqa) of this majāz is mentioning the part and intending the whole: he mentioned the striking of the neck and meant killing.
The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the words of the Exalted «حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها».
Here he borrowed "burdens" (awzār) for the implements of war and its heavy loads without which it cannot stand, such as weapons and horses. It may also be an implicit metaphor, by likening war to riding beasts carrying burdens, that is, heavy loads, while the affirmation of burdens is an imaginative attribution (takhyīl).

* Benefits:
- The rulings on jihad and captives..
The scholars differed over the ruling of this verse. Some said: it is abrogated by His words (فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ),
and by His words (فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ). This is the view of Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī and Ibn Jurayj. To it went al-Awzāʿī and the people of raʾy (the Ḥanafīs). They said: it is not permissible to show grace to a disbelieving captive, nor to ransom him; rather it is either killing or enslavement, whichever the imam sees fit. The author of al-Kashshāf transmitted from Mujāhid that he said: Today there is neither grace nor ransom; it is only Islam or the striking of the neck. Most scholars held that the verse is firmly established (muḥkama), and the imam has the choice, with regard to adult male disbelievers who have been captured, between killing them, enslaving them, showing them grace and releasing them without compensation, or ransoming them for money or for Muslim captives. To this went Ibn ʿUmar, and so said al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ and most of the Companions and scholars. It is the view of al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad and Isḥāq. Ibn ʿAbbās said: When the Muslims became many and their power grew strong, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed concerning the captives (فإما منّا بعد وإما فداء). This is the sound view, because it was the practice of the Prophet ﷺ and of the caliphs after him.
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ sent horsemen towards Najd, and they brought a man of the Banū Ḥanīfa called Thumāma, and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ went out to him and said: What do you have, Thumāma? He said: I have good, Muḥammad. If you kill, you kill one who has blood-guilt; if you show favour, you show favour to one who is grateful; and if you want money, ask and you will be given as much of it as you wish. The Prophet ﷺ left him. The next day he said to him: What do you have, Thumāma? He said the same as his first statement. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Release Thumāma. He went off to a palm grove near the mosque, washed, then entered the mosque and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. By Allah, there was nothing on earth more hateful to me than your face, and now your face has become the most beloved of faces to me. By Allah, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, and now your religion has become the most beloved of all religion to me. By Allah, there was no city more hateful to me than your city, and now your city has become the most beloved of all cities to me. Your horsemen seized me while I was intending the ʿumra, so what do you think? The Prophet ﷺ gave him good news and commanded him to perform the ʿumra. When he came to Mecca, someone said to him: Have you turned apostate? He said: No, but I have become a Muslim with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, not a grain of wheat will come to you from al-Yamāma until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permits it. Related by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
It is understood from His words the Exalted: حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها that jihad continues until the end of time. In the hadith, his words, peace be upon him: Jihad is ongoing from the time Allah sent me until the last of my community fights the Dajjāl.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is a vocative, an indefinite noun that is specified (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative. The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «تنصروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative; the clause «ينصركم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of the condition not joined by the fā'; and the clause «يثبّت ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) because the relative noun resembles a condition. (تعسا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. (لهم) is attached to (تعسا) «[Note: the lām has the meaning of transitivity; or the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: the punishment is for them.]». (الواو) is a conjunction, and the fāʿil (agent) of (أضلّ) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context. The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «(تعسوا) تعسا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين); and the clause «أضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the implied clause (تعسوا). 9- The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كرهوا..) is in the position of genitive through the «bāʾ», attached to an omitted word that is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(ما) is a relative in the position of accusative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الفاء) is a conjunction. The clause «ذلك بأنّهم كرهوا ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of the preceding supplication «[Note: or an explanatory resumption.]». The clause «كرهوا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ. The clause «أنزل الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). The clause «أحبط ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كرهوا.

* Morphology:
(تعسا) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb تعس of the باب فرح (pattern of فرح), meaning "he fell"; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa and sukūn.

* Benefits:
. The explanatory clause for the governor of the noun that has been left aside (al-ism al-mushtaghal ʿanhu).
For example: زيدا ضربته or زيدا ضربت أخاه. The clause ضربت explains the omitted verb implied before (زيد), meaning (ضربت زيدا ضربته). As for the words of the Exalted وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَتَعْساً لَهُمْ: الذين is a mubtadaʾ, and تعسا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb which is the khabar. (الذين) cannot be accusative through an omitted verb that (تعسا) explains, as you would say: زيدا ضربا إياه; and likewise it is not permissible to say: زيدا جدعا له, nor عمرا سقيا له. Rather you say with nominative: زيد جدعا له, and عمر سقيا له, because the lām is attached to the omitted verb and not to the maṣdar, since it does not govern through a preposition, and it is not the lām of reinforcement (lām al-taqwiya), because that is obligatory here, whereas the lām of reinforcement is not obligatory. And the words of the Exalted: سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ: if you take (من) to be redundant, then كم is a mubtadaʾ or a mafʿūl bihi of آتينا implied after it. And if you take it to be explicative of (كم), then it is a second mafʿūl bihi, fronted, of آتينا only. Like:
أعشرين درهما أعطيتك (Did I give you twenty dirhams?).

safi-cedvel:10-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām tawbīkhī). (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (في الأرض) is attached to (يسيروا). (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, the khabar of كان. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted word that is the ṣila of الذين. (عليهم) is attached to (دمّر), by including in it the meaning "covered" or "was angry" «[Note: in the lexicon: دمّره and دمّر عليه mean "He destroyed him" ... so there is no inclusion of meaning and no omission of an object.]», and the object of دمّر is omitted, i.e. their wealth and possessions. (الواو) is a conjunction. (للكافرين) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أمثالها). The clause «لم يسيروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Did they stay seated and not travel" The clause «ينظروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لم يسيروا. The clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative, the object of the verb of looking (naẓar) which is suspended by the interrogative, with an implied preposition. The clause «دمّر الله ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «للكافرين أمثالها» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause دمّر الله. 11- (ذلك بأنّ الله ... ) is like «ذلك بأنّهم» «[Note: in verse (9) of this sura.]». (لا) is the lā of generic negation (nāfiya li-l-jins). (لهم) is attached to the khabar of لا ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الكافرين ... ) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar in i'rab and in attachment. The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation of what precedes - or an explanatory resumption. The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا مولى لهم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(جنّات) is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension «[Note: the original is: He admits those who believe into gardens ...]», accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra. (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.]», with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath its trees. (الواو) is a conjunction in all three places. (ما) is a maṣdar particle ... (لهم) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (مثوى). The interpreted maṣdar (ما تأكل الأنعام) is in the position of genitive through the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is يأكلون. The clause «إنّ الله يدخل ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يدخل ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ. The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause. The clause «تجري ... » is in the position of accusative, an adjective of جنّات. The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause. The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين). The clause «يتمتّعون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين). The clause «يأكلون» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يتمتّعون. The clause «تأكل الأنعام» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما). The clause «النار مثوى لهم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The simile (al-tashbīh): in the words of the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَما تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعامُ وَالنَّارُ مَثْوىً لَهُمْ».
Here the disbelievers are likened to cattle in taking enjoyment through eating: they eat out of greed and voracity, as is the way of beasts, in contempt of them and belittling of their state, describing them as base and gluttonous, qualities which the Arabs censure and hate.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الذين كَفَرُواْ}: the nominative is permissible, as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the sentence from His saying «أضَلَّ أعمالَهم» as the khabar (predicate). The accusative is also permissible by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun), by an implied verb that «أضَلَّ» explains in meaning, that is: "He disappointed those who disbelieved."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the two aforementioned options are permissible here. The implied verb is: «رَحِمَ الذين آمنوا» ("He had mercy on those who believed").
His saying: {بِمَا نُزِّلَ على مُحَمَّدٍ}: the majority read it as a passive with shadda. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Miqsam read «نَزَّل» as an active verb, the agent being Allah the Exalted. al-Aʿmash read «أُنْزِل» with the hamza of transitivity, passive. «نَزَلَ» was also read as a triliteral active verb.
His saying: «وهو الحقُّ» is a parenthetical clause between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, or between the explained and the explainer. The explanation of «البال» was given earlier, in Sūrat Ṭāhā.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: there are two views. The more apparent is that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the preposition and its noun after it. The second, stated by al-Zamakhsharī, is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is that, because of such-and-such"; the preposition and its noun are then in the position of the accusative. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "There is no need for it."
His saying: «كذلك يَضْرِبُ»: al-Zamakhsharī analysed it as: "In the likeness of that striking [of a likeness], Allah strikes their likenesses for the people." The pronoun refers to the two groups, or to the people, in the sense that He strikes their likenesses for the sake of the people so that they may take heed.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ}: the operator in this adverbial is an implied verb, the same that operates on «ضَرْبَ الرِّقاب»; its implied form is: "so strike the necks at the time of your meeting the enemy." Abū l-Baqāʾ disallowed that the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself be the operator, saying: "because it is an emphasis." This is one of two views about a maṣdar standing in for its verb, as in «ضَرْباً زيداً»: is the operation attributed to it or to its operator? An example of it:
4050 - على حينَ أَلْهى الناسَ جُلُّ أمورِهمْ ... فنَدْلاً زُرَيْقُ المالَ نَدْلَ الثَّعالبِ
(At a time when most of their affairs had distracted the people, "Snatch, Zurayq, the wealth, as foxes snatch!")
«المالَ» is accusative either by «انْدُلْ» or by «نَدْلاً»; the maṣdar here is annexed to its object. This was used as evidence that the operation belongs to the maṣdar, because it is annexed to what follows it; had it not been an operator it would not have been annexed to what follows.
His saying: «حتى إذا»: this marks the end-point of the command to strike the necks. al-Sulamī read «فَشِدُّوا» with kasra on the shīn, which is very weak. «الوَثاق», with fatḥa (and also with kasra), is the noun for that with which something is tied.
His saying: {فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً}: there are two views about the two words. The better known is that both are accusative as maṣdars of a verb that may not be shown, because whenever a maṣdar is brought to detail the outcome of a sentence, it must be accusative by an implied verb that may not be shown. The implied form is: "either you grant a favour [of release] or you ransom with a ransom." Similar:
4051 - لأَجْهَدَنَّ فإمَّا دَرْءُ واقِعَةٍ ... تُخْشَى وإمَّا بلوغُ السُّؤْلِ والأَمَلِ
(I will surely strive; it will be either the warding off of a feared calamity or the attainment of wish and hope.)
The second view, stated by Abū l-Baqāʾ, is that both are mafʿūl bihi (direct objects) of an implied operator whose implied form is: "grant them a favour, and accept a ransom from them." The Shaykh said: "This is not a grammatical i'rab." Ibn Kathīr read «فِدَى» short. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is not permissible, because it is the maṣdar of «فادَيْتُه»." This is not to be heeded, because al-Farrāʾ reported four dialectal forms of it: the well-known one is with the long vowel; and the i'rab is «فداء لك»; also «فداءٍ» with the long vowel, indeclinable on kasra, with tanwīn, which is very strange. This resembles what some of them say: «هؤلاءٍ» with tanwīn; and «فِدى» with kasra and the short vowel, and «فَدَى» with fatḥa and the short vowel as well.
